title.ko: 개인정보의 국외 수집 및 이전에 관한 사항

rules.statement: Describe overseas collection and transfer (provision, access, outsourcing, storage) separately from domestic provision and outsourcing so the data subject clearly notices it.
When collecting directly from abroad (e.g. a foreign operator subject to PIPA collecting on foreign servers), list every country where the data is processed.

For each transfer (including onward transfer) state: legal basis (one item of PIPA 28-8(1)); items; destination countries, timing and method; recipient name (for a corporation, its name and contact); recipient's purpose and retention; how to refuse, the procedure, and the effect of refusing.

check.expr: every(section.S10.rows, r => r.basis && r.items && r.countries && r.timingMethod && r.recipient && r.recipientContact && r.purpose && r.retention) && exists(section.S10.refusal)

rules.statement: Where cloud use sends data to several countries, list all of them.
If the basis lies in another law, treaty or international agreement, name it and the article.
Overseas provision or outsourcing may be written only here if each row states its type (provision or outsourcing) and includes all S07 or S09 fields; then S07/S09 need not repeat it.
If data collected directly abroad is again provided, outsourced or stored abroad (including the same country), describe that transfer too.

basisOptionsInGuideline.label: other 28-8(1) items: not described in the guideline; route to legal review

goodPatterns: Heading 'overseas transfer'; a lead sentence citing PIPA 28-8(2) and stating refusal consequences and how to withdraw (e.g. membership cancellation path and call center).
One table per type (provision / outsourcing-storage): basis | items | countries | timing and method | recipient and contact | purpose | retention.
Examples of transfer types: HQ abroad consolidates or views Korean customer DB (provision); overseas call center subsidiary (outsourcing); backup to overseas servers (storage).

commonDefects.defect: Overseas cloud storage or API vendor not disclosed as a transfer.
Missing recipient contact, timing/method, or refusal method and effect.
Legal basis missing or not tied to a 28-8(1) item.
Only the vendor's HQ country listed while data sits in several regions.

extractionHints: overseas HQ, global CRM, offshore call center
foreign LLM or SaaS API names
withdrawal as the way to refuse transfer

needsVerification.note: Items of PIPA 28-8(1) other than 1 and 3 are not described in the guideline; do not generate their wording.
